The state government said investigations into the outbreak are ongoing, with health teams working to trace contacts of the confirmed cases and strengthen surveillance in affected communities. The National Cloud Infrastructure Strategy was announced as part of Nigeria's broader effort to formalize data-localization rules that require certain categories of data to be stored and processed within the country. Rather than treating these rules as barriers to investment, the government is positioning them as conditions that can be met by domestic and foreign technology providers, creating a structured market for cloud services.

Dr. Tijani said the strategy aims to address both security concerns and economic potential. By establishing clear standards for cloud infrastructure, the government hopes to attract private capital that can build and operate data centers, fiber networks, and related facilities within Nigeria. The approach is intended to reduce the cost of compliance for businesses while ensuring that sensitive data remains under Nigerian jurisdiction.

The initiative comes amid growing African demand for digital infrastructure as internet penetration rises and more government services move online. Several West African nations have introduced data-localization measures in recent years, but Nigeria's strategy is notable for its explicit focus on investment attraction. The government has indicated that it will offer policy incentives for investors who meet the data-sovereignty requirements, though specific fiscal details have not been disclosed.

Industry analysts said the success of the strategy will depend on the government's ability to balance regulatory certainty with the flexibility needed to attract competitive investment. The National Information Technology Development Agency has been directed to fast-track the implementation framework, including standards for cloud service providers, data-center licensing, and cross-border data-transfer conditions.

Speaking at a labour stakeholders' meeting, Edoka urged workers across the country to remain security-conscious and make informed political decisions that will protect their lives, jobs and welfare.

The labour adviser emphasized that the current security situation in Kogi State and across Nigeria poses a direct risk to the ability of workers to carry out their duties safely. He stated that without a secure environment, meaningful progress on workers' rights, wages and welfare cannot be achieved.

Edoka's comments come at a time when Nigeria's labour movement has been increasingly vocal about poor working conditions, unpaid wages and the need for better governance. The Special Adviser stressed that security is a prerequisite for any meaningful dialogue on labour issues, noting that workers cannot effectively advocate for their rights when their safety is at risk.

The meeting, which brought together labour leaders and stakeholders, served as a platform to discuss the intersection of security and workers' welfare. Edoka called on workers to be vigilant about the political choices they make, stating that their votes and political participation should prioritize candidates and parties that commit to improving the security situation.

While the Kogi State Government has not issued an official response to the adviser's comments, the warning highlights growing concerns about the impact of insecurity on economic activity and workers' wellbeing across Nigeria. The labour sector continues to grapple with multiple challenges, including unresolved minimum wage negotiations and poor working conditions, with insecurity now adding a new dimension to the discourse.

The adviser's remarks underscore a shifting narrative in Nigeria's labour landscape, where safety has increasingly superseded traditional concerns about wages and working conditions. In regions affected by banditry, kidnapping and communal violence, the simple act of reporting to work has become a hazardous endeavour. Edoka's warning reflects a reality where insecurity is not merely a background issue but a frontline determinant of employment viability.

Labour rights analysts note that when workers are compelled to prioritize survival over employment, the broader economy suffers. Productivity declines, informal sector growth accelerates and the formal workforce experiences heightened vulnerability. The Kogi State government's response to these security concerns will likely affect labour relations across the state and potentially set a precedent for other states facing similar challenges.

As Nigeria approaches another political cycle, Edoka's call for informed political decisions adds a new urgency to worker engagement. content:
Giovanni van Bronckhorst offered no excuses and refused to hide behind the harsh scoreline after Feyenoord's humiliating 5-1 defeat to Barcelona at the Camp Nou in their opening Champions League fixture. The Dutch coach spoke honestly, acknowledging Barcelona's quality while praising his young side's effort in a night that will live long in the memory of Feyenoord supporters.

The defeat leaves Feyenoord with a mountain to climb in Group C, but van Bronckhorst was keen to extract what positives he could from a performance that saw Barcelona race into a 3-0 lead before the Dutch side managed a consolation through Antoni Milambo just before half-time.

"We played against the best team in the world tonight," van Bronckhorst said in his post-match press conference. "Barcelona were superior in every department. There are no excuses. We have to tip our hat to them."

The Catalan giants dominated from the first whistle. Fermín López opened the scoring in the 12th minute, before Raphinha doubled the lead just before the half-hour mark. Robert Lewandowski added a third before the break, leaving Feyenoord facing a mountain at 3-0 down. The Dutch side pulled one back just before half-time when Milambo netted a consolation, but Barcelona quickly restored their three-goal cushion early in the second half through Lamine Yamal.

Yamal, who turned 17 last July, became the youngest scorer in Champions League history when he found the net, and his performance earned high praise from the Feyenoord boss.

"He is exceptional," van Bronckhorst said of the Barcelona youngster. "He has all the qualities to win the Ballon d'Or one day. He is the best in the world at his age and I see a great future for him."

The Barcelona youngster's goal came just four minutes after Milampo's consolation, as the 17-year-old latched onto a through-ball and slotted beyond the advancing Feyenoord keeper. The goal effectively sealed the contest, though Feyenoord pulled another back late through Calvin Stengs.

"We gave everything," van Bronckhorst said. "But against a team with that level of quality, individual moments and collective precision make the difference. We have to learn from this and move on."

Barcelona's victory was built on a clinical first half and sustained pressure after the break. Lewandowski's close-range finish put the hosts 3-0 up, and although Milambo's goal offered a brief glimmer of hope, Yamal's strike and a late strike from substitute Ferran Torres — who made it 5-1 — underscored the gulf in class.

For Feyenoord, the result represents a tough reality check in Europe's premier club competition. The Dutch side, who finished third in the Eredivisie last season, will need to regroup quickly if they are to salvage any pride in the competition. Their next fixture sees them face Atletico Madrid at the Rotterdam stadium, a match van Bronckhorst will use to assess how his side respond to adversity.

"The most important thing is how we react," the Feyenoord coach said. "We have a long season ahead and we have to make sure we learn from nights like this. Barcelona were the best in the world tonight, and we have to accept that."

Barcelona, meanwhile, will take confidence from a comprehensive win that signals their intent in this season's Champions League. With Yamal continuing to break records and establish himself as one of Europe's most exciting young talents, the Spanish side will be hoping he can keep delivering moments of magic on the biggest stages.

The result leaves Group C wide open, but Barcelona's commanding performance has put them in a strong position to advance. For Feyenoord, the focus now shifts to domestic action and ensuring this result does not derail their Eredivisie campaign.

Van Bronckhorst's admission that Barcelona were the best in the world on the night is likely to resonate beyond this single fixture. His prediction that Yamal will one day win the Ballon d'Or adds a fascinating subplot to a season in which the teenage forward is already making his mark on Europe's top competition.

"He has everything," van Bronckhorst said. "Yamal is going to be a huge name in world football."

excerpt: The Nigeria Police Force National Cybercrime Centre has arrested a 27-year-old woman, Hafsat Abubakar, in connection with the creation and circulation of a forged document falsely suggesting that fintech company OPay Nigeria Limited was shutting down its...
content:
The Nigeria Police Force National Cybercrime Centre has arrested a 27-year-old woman, Hafsat Abubakar, in connection with the creation and circulation of a forged document falsely suggesting that fintech company OPay Nigeria Limited was shutting down its operations. The arrest was announced on Tuesday, September 9, 2026, following the emergence of the fraudulent notice that circulated on social media platforms.

According to the police command, the forged document claimed that OPay was ceasing operations effective immediately, causing panic among users and traders who rely on the platform for financial transactions. The notice, which bore the OPay logo and appeared official, was shared widely across WhatsApp groups and Twitter before the error was detected.

Hafsat Abubakar was paraded alongside other suspects at the command’s headquarters in Abuja. The National Cybercrime Centre traced the origin of the document to her, stating that she created the fake notice with the intent to cause public panic and tarnish the reputation of the fintech firm. The police said investigations revealed that the motive was not financial gain but rather to create confusion in the digital payment space.

OPay Nigeria Limited released a statement on the same day denying that it was shutting down. The company said it remained fully operational and that its services were functioning normally. The firm thanked the police for the swift response and urged the public to disregard any unofficial information about its operations.

The arrest comes at a time when digital financial services in Nigeria have seen rapid growth, with OPay among the leading platforms for mobile money, ride-hailing, and food delivery. Cybersecurity experts have warned that the rise of fintech platforms has also attracted individuals seeking to exploit public trust through misinformation. The police command said it would continue to monitor for similar incidents and urged members of the public to verify information through official channels.

Legal analysts noted that the charge against Abubakar could fall under Nigeria’s Cybercrime (Prohibition, Prevention, etc.) Act, which prohibits the creation and distribution of forged electronic documents. If convicted, she could face significant penalties including fines and imprisonment. The police have not yet disclosed the specific charges preferred, but said the case would be prosecuted to serve as a deterrent to others who might consider similar acts.

The Nation Newspaper reported that Lagos State had recorded 53 suspected cases of diphtheria in 2026, including six laboratory-confirmed cases, though this development was unrelated to the OPay arrest. The state government had assured residents that there was no widespread outbreak of the disease.

The investigation into the forged OPay notice remains ongoing. The police said they were examining whether Abubakar acted alone or had collaborators, and whether the fake notice was part of a broader campaign to destabilize digital financial services in the country.

title: AI Agents Are Changing How People Work — And the Shift Is Only Beginning
author: AI News Factory Desk
excerpt: AI agents are moving beyond simple chat interfaces and becoming capable of completing increasingly complex tasks across work and business.
content: Artificial intelligence is entering another phase of its evolution as AI agents become increasingly capable of performing multi-step tasks rather than simply responding to individual prompts.

The change matters because agents can potentially connect reasoning with actions. Instead of asking a system a question and manually carrying out the result, users can increasingly delegate parts of a workflow to software.

Businesses are watching the development closely as companies explore how agentic systems could assist with research, customer service, software development, analysis and other knowledge-intensive work.
The technology remains imperfect. Reliability, security, privacy and the ability to verify automated decisions remain important challenges.
For users, the larger story is not simply about smarter chatbots. It is about software becoming more capable of taking action on a person's behalf.

title: The Global Technology Shift Everyone Should Be Watching
author: AI News Factory Desk
excerpt: Technology is becoming increasingly embedded in everyday infrastructure, changing how people communicate, work and access information.
content: Technology is no longer limited to the devices people carry. Increasingly, software and connected systems are becoming part of the infrastructure behind everyday life.
Cloud computing, artificial intelligence, automation and increasingly capable connected devices are reshaping the way organisations operate.
The pace of change also creates new questions around security, privacy and access.
For consumers and businesses alike, understanding these shifts may become as important as adopting the technology itself.

title: What AI Could Mean for the Next Business Cycle
author: AI News Factory Business Desk
excerpt: Companies are increasingly treating artificial intelligence as an operational technology rather than simply an experimental tool.
content: Artificial intelligence is becoming a strategic consideration for businesses across industries.
The focus is gradually moving from experimentation toward practical questions about productivity, costs, customer experience and competitive advantage.
That transition could make the coming years important for companies deciding where AI should be deployed and where human oversight must remain central.
The strongest results may come from organisations that treat AI as part of a broader operating strategy rather than as a standalone technology.

title: Why Scientific Discoveries Still Matter in a Fast-Moving World
author: AI News Factory Science Desk
excerpt: Scientific research continues to shape medicine, technology and our understanding of the world around us.
content: Scientific progress rarely happens overnight. Many major advances emerge from years of experiments, observations and incremental discoveries.
That process can make science difficult to communicate in a world increasingly driven by rapid news cycles.
Yet the implications of scientific research can extend far beyond the original discovery, influencing medicine, engineering, environmental policy and future technologies.
Understanding the evidence behind a discovery is therefore just as important as understanding the headline.

title: How Information Shapes the Modern World
author: AI News Factory World Desk
excerpt: The speed at which information travels is changing how societies understand events as they happen.
content: Information now travels across borders within seconds, creating unprecedented access to events happening around the world.
That speed has advantages, but it also creates challenges. Early reports can change as additional evidence becomes available.
For readers, distinguishing between confirmed information, developing reports and speculation is increasingly important.
A modern newsroom therefore has to do more than publish quickly. It must also provide context and clearly communicate uncertainty.
